roadmap.goal: Deliver GH #295: cut VmDriver::new to its accepted seven-argument gate-coupled shape (F-01), stand up the node-shared guest-network owner (shared bridge, TCX classifier plus proof-mark guard, constant nft rules, two node-owned transparent listeners), and activate independently approved DISTILL evidence (S-ND295-00..37, B-ND295-T1-BASE/T1-PORT4) across overdrive-core/control-plane/worker/dataplane/netlink/sim/cli in roadmap order. Revised 02-01 remains blocked while the newly authored S-ND295-00/10/11/12/13 bodies await independent DISTILL and roadmap review. Delivery closes with the production-composed walking skeleton, recurring conformance, and two attachment-capacity receipts.
roadmap.estimate_basis: Phase 01 lands the single dependency-neutral API cut that every gate-coupled scaffold needs (8h). Phase 02 builds three acyclic production slices in dependency order -- the complete shared-switch attachment owner with its classifier, typed TCX lifecycle, and semantic bridge guard (48h); IP-family constant-rule replacement/rollback (10h); and listener/capability lifecycle (30h). The phase-02 total remains 88h; the 2026-09-20 remediation redistributes the prior 28h/30h split so no owner step consumes later-step effects. Phase 03 activates the gate/release/recovery acceptance bodies against those owners (18h + 16h + 26h). Phase 04 proves the whole cut end-to-end on native metal: the walking skeleton (24h), the recurring conformance suite (10h), non-regression plus the Tier-3 timed double-loss scenario (16h), and the two T1 benchmark receipts (8h).
delivery_protocol: Execute in the fixed dependency order 01-01 -> 02-01 -> 02-02 -> 02-03 -> 03-01 -> 03-02 -> 03-03 -> 04-01 -> 04-02 -> 04-03 -> 04-04; every phase-02/03 step needs the shared-owner surface the prior step left compiling.

Every step activates only the reasoned-#[ignore] bodies its scenario_ids name. A crafter may not weaken, replace, re-author, or repair an acceptance body authored in DISTILL -- only remove the reasoned-pending marker and supply the implementation the body already specifies.

The feature delta (feature-delta.md) pins the exact public/private contract, including every doc-hidden port. Any new public method, type, port, error variant, or persisted field beyond what feature-delta.md names is a blocker -- surface it, do not improvise a shape (root CLAUDE.md, 'Implement to the design').

Each step's crafter runs the Lima-routed compile/clippy/nextest gates named in its verification list before requesting review; each reviewer records deliver/review-<step-id>.md with APPROVED before advancement.
Mutation testing (cargo xtask mutants) is the single final DELIVER gate after every roadmap step and review per .claude/rules/testing.md -- it is never run per step.

Tier-3/native-metal bodies in phases 02-04 run only through cargo xtask metal run -- (or cargo xtask lima run -- for non-KVM Lima-root Tier-2/Tier-3 portions); no Tier-3 evidence is accepted from a virtualized or nested host.

criteria: GuestNetworkExecWiring::new(clock) / gate() / supervisor() construct one private mutex/Notify state that starts BootClosed with zero active claims and no recovery snapshot; GuestNetworkExecGate, GuestNetworkExecSupervisor, and GuestNetworkExecClaim are each private-field, non-`Clone` types whose only cloneable handle is their own `Arc`, and none is constructible outside GuestNetworkExecWiring.

GuestNetworkExecGate::claim_release returns Some(claim) and increments the active-claim count only from Open; from BootClosed or Recovering it registers a Notify waiter before unlocking and retries after wake without touching any VM pending-EXEC state; from FailStop it returns None immediately; GuestNetworkExecClaim's Drop decrements the count under the same lock and wakes waiters.

GuestNetworkExecSupervisor::open_after_boot performs only BootClosed -> Open, wakes waiters, and returns false from every other state; is_boot_closed is the read-only precondition check used immediately before fresh-process mutation and is never treated as a runtime health signal; begin_recovery performs only Open -> Recovering and returns true only for the winning transition; complete_attempt applies only while Recovering, updates the first-remaining component or transitions to Open and wakes waiters, and returns false after Open/FailStop so late work cannot overwrite either; recovery_progress returns a value snapshot only while Recovering and None in every other state; fail_stop atomically transitions BootClosed/Open/Recovering -> FailStop, returns the one request to send on its first call and None on every later call (first-request-wins, idempotent-send), and wakes waiters. (This enumeration of GuestNetworkExecSupervisor's surface is non-exhaustive -- see feature-delta.md for the complete method list.)

VmDriver::new's signature is exactly `pub fn new(vmm: Arc<dyn Vmm>, clock: Arc<dyn Clock>, fs: Arc<dyn CgroupFs>, cgroup_accounting: Arc<dyn CgroupAccounting>, probe_runner: Arc<ProbeRunner>, guest_network_exec: Arc<GuestNetworkExecGate>, layout: VmHostLayout) -> Self` with no optional builder, no default-open gate constructed inside VmDriver, and no change to the public Driver trait.

release_for_exit_emission acquires a gate claim strictly before it reads pending_exec or gate_sender; an Open claim is held through the beacon-writer acknowledgement; a Recovering caller waits without taking either value and proceeds only once recovery reopens the gate; a FailStop caller is woken with None so EXEC is never taken or written and process shutdown owns the remaining VMM/gate teardown; an already-written command is never paused or frozen.

steps.implementation_notes: Property-based tests (proptest) and state-delta thinking (assert on a declared universe of what changed vs. what's asserted unchanged) take priority over single-example unit tests where the contract supports it; integration/E2E stays single-example since it verifies wiring, not invariants. STAGE CONTEXT (cascade): NEW code = Stage 0 (paradigm-from-day-zero, no debt accumulates). This repository's actual suite is Rust (nextest/proptest/DST per .claude/rules/testing.md), not Python/Hypothesis; translate the mandate's INTENT into Rust terms: the GuestNetworkExecGate/Supervisor state machine is exactly the 'bounded-change' Contract Shape the feature delta already assigns it (gate state is read-only; the allowed delta is active-claim count +/-1 and waiter registration/wake) -- drive it with seeded proptest schedules over BootClosed/Open/Recovering/FailStop transitions plus a whole-private-state-delta assertion that nothing outside that declared universe (recovery snapshot, request channel, pending EXEC values, other claims) changed, per the Effect Isolation and Contract Shape classification table in feature-delta.md. Do not invent this state machine's public surface beyond the exact code fence under 'EXEC-close linearization' in feature-delta.md -- if a transition case is underspecified there, stop and surface it rather than adding a method the design did not name. The GuestNetworkProvisioner/SharedGuestNetworkOwner trait declarations this step also lands are pure compile-time API surface (todo!() RED-scaffold bodies) -- do not invent real startup/converge/audit/quiesce behavior for them here; that is step 02-01's job.

steps.name: Complete shared-switch owner with classifier, TCX, and bridge guard
steps.description: Complete the one production shared-switch attachment slice. Land A2/pool, the one owner, D5 scratch algorithm, D12 lifecycle/inventory plus its private projection source, D12A's production allocation leaf seam, classifier/maps, D6, D9, and D13's existing VmHostState/telemetry plus ordering-honest Sim sweep oracle. criteria: AllocationSpec deletes netns/host_veth and its six separate guest-network option fields and gains exactly `pub network: Option<GuestNetworkAssignment>` where GuestNetworkAssignment is `{ address: Ipv4Addr, tap: String, mac: [u8; 6], gateway: Ipv4Addr, prefix: u8, dns: Ipv4Addr }`; VmNetworkAttachment stays exactly `{ tap: String, mac: [u8; 6] }` and CloudHypervisorVmm renders `--net tap=...,mac=...` directly, removing the `ip netns exec` launch-tool prerequisite; both types keep their existing Debug/Clone/PartialEq/Eq derives and add no serde/rkyv schema, generation, or listener-port field.

GuestAddressPool exposes exactly `assign`, `release`, `snapshot` under one parking_lot::Mutex critical section, none crossing `.await`; assign is atomic and idempotent for an already-held AllocationId (returns the byte-equal existing plan) and otherwise inserts the smallest free non-reserved address, excluding prefix-network/broadcast/gateway addresses; release of an absent allocation is an idempotent no-op; snapshot returns a detached BTreeMap clone in allocation-ID order; below-cap exhaustion returns `GuestNetworkError::PoolExhausted { held, capacity }`, never a panic or address reuse.

`overdrive_control_plane::guest_network::GuestNetworkProvisioner` is exactly the two-method async trait `provision(&self, plan: &GuestNetworkPlan) -> Result<()>` / `teardown(&self, plan: &GuestNetworkPlan) -> Result<()>`; GuestNetworkPlan is `#[doc(hidden)] pub` with private fields and exactly four read-only accessors (alloc/bridge/node_prefix/assignment); production construction and the HostGuestNetworkProvisioner implementation remain private to overdrive-control-plane; overdrive-sim implements only the public port. (The trait signature itself, per C-295-G, was already declared as compile-time API surface in step 01-01; this step supplies HostGuestNetworkProvisioner's real production body.)

Ordinary handler -> reconciler -> action-shim start/restart/stop dispatch uses the same one SharedGuestNetworkOwner object that boot composed; dispatch_with_guest_network_provisioner_for_test and run_convergence_tick_with_guest_network_provisioner_for_test execute that identical workflow-intent preflight, hydration, View write-through, action shim, re-enqueue, and error projection, differing only in the one injected driven-network adapter. The production HostNetworkProvisioner/NetSlot/netns/veth branch, AppState::net_slot_allocator, boot adoption, deleted shim error variants, setns VMM launch, and optional compatibility path are absent after this cut.

SharedGuestNetworkOwner is exactly `probe_startup`, `sweep_stale`, `converge_shared`, `audit_shared` (returning SharedGuestNetworkAuditError), and `quiesce_managed_taps`, all on the one concrete production owner that also implements the inherited GuestNetworkProvisioner allocation operations -- no second owner object exists for boot/runtime ownership versus allocation provision/teardown. (The trait signature was likewise declared in step 01-01; this step supplies HostSharedGuestNetworkOwner's real method bodies behind it, replacing 01-01's todo!() scaffold.)

The private HostSharedGuestNetworkOwner startup algorithm, driven through the module-private SharedGuestNetworkScratchIo seam by source-local tests (not the public SimSharedGuestNetworkOwner), proves: probe_startup owns only isolated scratch resources and always attempts their cleanup; on primary-probe failure with successful cleanup the primary typed error returns and the scratch complement is exactly zero; on cleanup failure or non-empty cleanup read-back, startup still refuses with EXEC BootClosed and no production owner/task is published, while preserving both the primary and cleanup errors plus the complete GuestNetworkScratchComplement with any unread-back resource family reported Unavailable, never fabricated zero; a later retry or boot never overwrites that first-failure evidence.

The node bridge MAC is set only from `overdrive_core::dataplane::GUEST_BRIDGE_MAC = [0x02, 0x01, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x01]`, never adopted from ambient kernel state; convergence creates-or-adopts a bridge-kind link, brings it down, sets the fixed MAC, reads back exact name/ifindex/type/MAC/gateway-prefix, then brings it up before writing any endpoint entry or attaching any TAP; a successful mutation followed by wrong read-back is `GuestNetworkError::PostconditionMismatch` and refuses startup.

The C-295-0 SCHED_CLS classifier attaches at TCX ingress with first ordering to every managed TAP against one 65,536-entry ifindex-keyed endpoint map containing exactly source IPv4, source MAC, and bridge MAC; its exact eight counter classes and every Ethernet/ARP/TCP partition produce the accepted TC_ACT_OK/TC_ACT_SHOT, proof mark, MAC rewrite, original-destination preservation, and single-counter result. Existing S-ND295-08/09 BPF_PROG_TEST_RUN plus real-kernel no-escape evidence is activated in this step.

D-295-DISTILL-6 remains exactly GuestTcxAttachment, GuestTcxCounter, TcxAttachPoint, GuestTcxError, its semantic program_ids, and five doc-hidden free functions. D12 adds only exact doc-hidden GuestTcxObject/GuestTcxEndpoint, semantic map shapes with opaque unsupported tokens, GuestTcxMapSchema/GuestTcxInventoryFamily/GuestTcxInventoryCapture/GuestTcxInventoryIdentity, and opaque non-Clone GuestTcxProgram/GuestTcxLink/GuestTcxAdoptedState fences. No lifecycle trait, generic command, raw aya/numeric ABI, new inventory ownership ID, FD/record, ELF name, or additional free operation crosses into control-plane.

GuestTcxProgram::load(&GuestTcxInventoryIdentity)/pin_endpoint_map/pin_counter_map/insert_endpoint/read_endpoint/attach_first_ingress and GuestTcxLink::program_id/pin/detach are the only live-loader methods. GuestTcxAdoptedState::for_inventory(&GuestTcxInventoryIdentity, link_pin) plus its exact adopt/read/unpin methods is the only adoption surface. HostSharedGuestNetworkOwner::new remains sole constructor and retains one Mutex<Option<private HostGuestTcxState { program, inventory }>>; Sim implements only the high-level owner. Load preserves aya::EbpfError; semantic errors remain source-less; cleanup, Drop non-mutation, read-back, and no-lock-across-await match D12.

GuestTcxMapKind is exactly Hash, Array, or Unsupported(opaque token); key/value/capacity are likewise closed semantic shapes with equality-preserving opaque unsupported properties. Tokens have no public constructor/accessor and render no raw/numeric identity. Endpoint schema is exactly Hash/U32/EndpointAbi/EndpointMaximum and counter schema Array/U32/CounterU64/CounterSlots. MapSchemaMismatch carries comparable expected/observed GuestTcxMapSchema and no source; aya kind-decode failure remains sourced Map. Raw sizes/capacity never cross into control-plane.

GuestTcxInventoryIdentity::capture always returns GuestTcxInventoryCapture. into_parts moves an observation-capable identity and one Result disposition: capture exhausts map/program/link domains in fixed order, stores failed-domain flags privately in the identity, and moves the original first Map/Program error directly. Real D5 stores identity before moving disposition into the TcxLoad primary and skips BPF load on Err. The identity never stores/clones/wraps that source; affected later families return source-less CaptureUnavailable, while independent successful domains and exact pin paths remain observable.

After explicit cleanup and handle release, D5 maps its eight count_tcx families exactly to observe_endpoint_maps/observe_counter_maps/observe_endpoint_entries/observe_tcx_programs/observe_tcx_links/observe_endpoint_map_pins/observe_counter_map_pins/observe_tcx_link_pins. Dataplane uses complete loaded-object enumeration, private by-ID entry lookup, and exact pins. Only a recorded receipt may return an owned nonzero count. With no receipt and a complete baseline, zero candidates is Ok(0), but any candidate—including a unique semantic match—is source-less InventoryAmbiguous; failed baseline is CaptureUnavailable. Every Err becomes Unavailable, first-source retention and later-family continuation remain D5-owned, and pin absence or Drop never implies object absence.

D12's raw map/program/link/pin observations, GuestTcxInventorySource trait, AyaGuestTcxInventorySource implementation, capture_with_source, and project_map_kind/project_map_schema are dataplane-private. Public capture delegates to the real source and retains it privately. Source-local tests inject only capture_with_source with raw aya/numeric observations and domain failures, proving every supported/unsupported semantic projection and source branch; opaque public tokens retain no constructor/accessor and no raw value crosses crates.

The D-295-DISTILL-9 bridge adapter is real kernel-backed, not process-local. It owns the already-approved semantic BridgeGuardSpec/fact/inventory/outcome/error types and exactly observe, converge_table, converge_chain, converge_set, converge_rules, insert_member, delete_member, delete_rules, delete_set, delete_chain, delete_table, and delete_owned_guard over the one private family-aware nft codec; existing IPv4 operations remain byte-equal. The one table bridge overdrive-mtls guard has one managed_taps ifname set, one filter/prerouting/-300/accept chain, exactly the three ordered proof-mark rules, exact-exclusive aggregate deletion, and complete foreign/conflict preservation.

The shared-switch owner pins maps and per-TAP links only under /sys/fs/bpf/overdrive/mtls-endpoints/{maps/{endpoints,counters},links/<tap>-ingress}; provision orders down TAP -> bridge/master -> guard membership -> endpoint insertion -> TCX first-ingress attach/pin/query and exact program/ifindex/pin/MAC read-back before VMM start. Closing loader handles never detaches a pinned link, and no pin outside that hierarchy is adopted.

provision/teardown mutate only the named allocation's TAP/master/up state, endpoint entry, TCX link/pin, and bridge-guard membership (plus shared bridge/maps/guard only toward their one desired identity). Teardown deletes endpoint, unpins/detaches TCX, deletes the TAP while guard membership remains, removes membership, proves the named complement empty without changing an unrelated attachment, and releases the address last; typed normal-path failures are never hidden by Drop.

D12A adds one module-private GuestNetworkAllocationIo leaf interface used by the real owner, with exact tap mutate/observe, D9 member mutate/observe, and D12/D6 endpoint/link mutate/observe methods. HostGuestNetworkAllocationIo is the sole real adapter over a shared Arc<Mutex<Option<HostGuestTcxState>>>; the owner publishes a private alloc->{ifindex,program_id} record only after final read-back; with_allocation_io is source-local cfg(test)-only. Tests invoke real provision/teardown, inject only leaf results, and record calls; no public hook, simulated action owner, completed result, or replacement workflow exists.

D12A TAP observation is exactly Absent{name}, Incompatible{name,ifindex,kind,persistent,up,owner_uid,master_ifindex}, or Persistent{name,ifindex,up,owner_uid,master_ifindex}. The real leaf maps the existing typed persistent-TAP observer plus doc-hidden semantic link identity; the owner alone constructs GuestNetworkFact::Tap/LinkMaster and requires persistent TAP, exact OVERDRIVE_VMM_UID, desired up/down, stable ifindex, and exact master. Absent/incompatible are semantic PostconditionMismatch, never fabricated Netlink errors.

GuestNetworkAllocationIo::observe_bridge returns private Absent{name} or Present{name,ifindex,kind}; the real leaf performs generic semantic link lookup and the owner compares through GuestNetworkFact::BridgeLinkIdentity. It refreshes immediately before both down-TAP and final up-TAP master checks, uses only a Bridge-kind current ifindex as expected master, and never caches ownership. Scripted tests return actual facts, not boolean success; raw LinkMessage/details and a public bridge port are forbidden.

Provision succeeds only after TAP create/down/master observations, full guard membership, exact endpoint read-back, first-ingress attach/pin/query/pin presence, and final TAP-up observation. Primary failure drives owner rollback. Teardown/rollback continue endpoint -> pinned/pending link -> endpoint/link/pin absence read-back while TAP exists -> TAP down -> guarded TAP delete -> guard delete -> final TAP/guard read-back, retaining first cleanup source; only empty complement succeeds and address release follows outside. Source-local S06/S11/S12 fail every leaf/wrong read-back and assert continuation/no-release/retry/unrelated preservation; Lima retains actual effects.

D13 retains mandatory vm_host_state before shared_guest_network in both helpers and the approved guest_network.shared_owner_boot_phase telemetry. For the first honest RED, SimSharedGuestNetworkOwner::with_sweep_host_state receives the same SimVmHostState and records SimSharedGuestNetworkSweepCall { call_index, host } at the actual sweep_stale call while preserving the existing calls() API. No ServerConfig override, boot port, alternate owner, product hook, or public state accessor is added; production events remain separate GREEN telemetry.

Before changing source order, reclamation_completes_before_stale_shared_network_sweep_for_every_seeded_prior_vm must fail through current composition because the real sweep-call snapshot still contains seeded host residue, with the replay seed printed; it must not depend on absent D13 events. Only that RED authorizes reclamation-before-sweep. GREEN separately proves approved event order, and native metal independently proves the real VMM/kernel complement and first lease acceptance.

DISTILL must extend S00 through D12's private source, author S10, drive S11/S12 through D12A, and complete S13 with the sweep-call RED plus separate telemetry/native layers. Crafters may activate approved bodies but may not author substitute assertions, expose private seams, or replace production owners.

S-ND295-00, S-ND295-02..04, and S-ND295-06..13 are this step's activation set. S-ND295-05 remains exclusively in step 03-01. No acceptance assertion is weakened, replaced, or re-authored; transitioned Contract Shape metadata names only the grouped network delta and every active acceptance body retains its outcome anchor.

steps.description: Implement MtlsInterceptWorker's node-shared listener lifecycle (start_shared_owner/wait_shared_owner_failure/converge_shared_owner/audit_shared_owner/shutdown_owner plus per-allocation start_alloc/stop_alloc) over C-295-L, and the module-private D-295-DISTILL-7 CapabilityRegistry state machine (checked generation, Pending/Active/Retiring, RAII claims, publication fence, scoped drain, address-reuse exclusion) with GEN-295-A's checked_add(1)-then-publish generation ownership and PORT-295-C's userspace source/destination registry. criteria: The node listener owner binds exactly one leg-F and one leg-C transparent TCP listener that survive every allocation stop and close only with their node owner; they are ordinary node-owned sockets recreated at boot, never pinned/adopted per-allocation state.

start_shared_owner captures observe_shared, binds F and C once at the boot owner boundary, records both concrete non-zero SocketAddrV4 values, calls converge_shared with the captured prior identity, retains its node-scoped guard, starts exactly two accept tasks, and audits both socket and rule identities before returning; a partial bind/rule/task-start failure closes every listener, rule guard, and task acquired by that invocation and refuses boot without ever publishing a half-started owner.

Leg F resolves the accepted socket's validated source guest address to an immutable (AllocationId, generation, SpiffeId) capability and separately recovers the original destination; leg C resolves the recovered destination IPv4 to one destination registration, requires the recovered TCP port in allowed_ports, then captures that capability; unknown IP or disallowed port closes fail-closed; an accepted predecessor connection is never re-looked-up or re-attributed to an address-reuse successor.

CapabilityRegistry::begin_registration performs checked_add(1) before any reservation or kernel effect (returning MtlsInterceptInstallError::GenerationExhausted { next: u64::MAX } with no registry/nft effect on overflow, u64::MAX never minted), then atomically reserves the allocation/source/destination keys as Pending; a conflicting Pending/Active/Retiring key returns RegistrationConflict before element acquisition.

PendingCapability::activate re-enters the lock: if still Pending it moves guards into the record, transitions Pending -> Active, publishes claimable source/destination indexes atomically, wakes waiters, and returns Activated; if retirement already owns the generation it moves guards into the Retiring record, publishes no index, and returns Retired -- and MtlsInterceptWorker::start_alloc projects Retired to exactly `MtlsInterceptInstallError::RegistrationRetired { alloc_id }`, never Ok(()), with stage projection `"registration_retired"`.

CapabilityClaim::publish re-enters the lock: Active stores the handle then decrements in-flight and returns Published; Retiring decrements/wakes and returns Retired(handle) with the worker awaiting teardown outside the lock; no returned handle is ever re-looked-up or attributed to a successor.

begin_retire is idempotent and marks the exact record/generation Retiring, removing claimable indexes immediately for Active or transferring retirement ownership for Pending; wait_for_claims holds no mutex while waiting and yields CapabilityDrain only once in_flight == 0 and the pending-owner flag is clear; stop_alloc drains only that generation's handles/elements via CapabilityDrain::take_handles/take_elements/complete, removes the recorded 2+P nft elements with read-back, tears down TAP/TCX/guard membership, and releases the address last -- unrelated handles/capabilities and both shared listeners remain live throughout.

Address reuse is remove-before-reassign: predecessor registrations and its active generation are gone before successor registration is accepted; a successor using the same address is refused until the predecessor's drain completes.

A production-path test (or focused integration case) holds real enforcement across a retirement race after claim, returns a real handle, and observes awaited teardown with zero publication -- closing the one race Part D's spike evidence did not execute.

shutdown_owner closes both listener admissions, retires all exact capabilities, waits every in-flight claim, drains every published handle, removes their allocation elements, joins both accept tasks, closes both listener sockets, then deliberately relinquishes the node-scoped shared-rule guard without deleting the constant rules/empty sets, preserving the listenerless mark/local-route fail-closed state until next-boot revalidation.

S-ND295-20..26 (two-listener owner start, atomic capability/port membership, generation exhaustion, late-handle fence, address reuse, isolated allocation stop, and owner shutdown) are activated against the real registry and worker, including the D-295-DISTILL-7 model tables and Tier-3 real-listener/enforcement cases for S-ND295-25 -- no acceptance body is weakened, replaced, or re-authored.

steps.name: Attachment-capacity benchmark receipts: T1-BASE and T1-PORT4
steps.description: Produce the two required, non-EDD measurement receipts under target/benchmarks/netns-density-295/{T1-BASE,T1-PORT4}/ via a new DELIVER benchmark target that drives 16,384 real production-owner network attachments (T1-BASE: N=16,384/M=0, Job-shaped, no VMM population, no Service TCP listeners; T1-PORT4: N=16,384/M=65,536, Service-shaped with TCP ports 8080/8081/8443/9000, no VMM population) and reports the exact CAP-295-A/PORT-295-C element inventory, memory, update, and sweep measurements.
criteria: T1-BASE attaches exactly 16,384 Job-shaped allocation network attachments through the real production GuestNetworkProvisioner/SharedGuestNetworkOwner (no VMM population, no Service TCP listeners) and reports: successful attach/read-back for all 16,384; kernel memory delta for every map/set/link/FDB; full-population insert/delete elements/s; one outbound-hit packet per source plus 256 deterministic missing-source probes with exact lookup packets/s and counters; and a full 3N+M=49,152-element sweep wall time with an empty complement afterward -- IP-set inventory 2N+M=32,768, bridge managed_taps inventory N=16,384.

T1-PORT4 attaches exactly 16,384 Service-shaped allocation network attachments each with TCP ports 8080, 8081, 8443, and 9000 (no VMM population) and reports the same memory/update/sweep measurement classes plus one hit for all four ports and one 9001-miss for every destination (81,920 lookup packets total), exact counters and packets/s, and a full sweep/read-back complement -- IP-set inventory 2N+M=98,304, bridge managed_taps inventory N=16,384, total 114,688 elements.

Both receipts report the actual measured N, M, port distribution, kernel version (uname -r), and any substrate limit encountered -- no receipt asserts or implies a simultaneous-connection, EnforcedConnection, throughput, RLIMIT_NOFILE, pids.max, threads-max, or connection-pump capacity claim; CAP-295-A's attachment-only boundary is stated explicitly in the receipt output.

The benchmark target is clearly marked non-EDD (not under verification/expectations/, not asserted against in a pass/fail nextest body) and is driven only through the real production owner -- no fixture manufactures kernel state the production path would not itself create.

Both receipts are produced on the same native x86_64 metal lease class used by phase 04's other Tier-3 evidence, via cargo xtask metal run --, and are committed under target/benchmarks/netns-density-295/{T1-BASE,T1-PORT4}/ (or, if target/ is gitignored, the raw captured output is preserved as evidence alongside the roadmap per the verification.md discipline for executed, non-narrated measurement).
verification: cargo xtask metal run -- cargo run -p overdrive-control-plane --bin netns_density_benchmark --features integration-tests -- --profile t1-base --out target/benchmarks/netns-density-295/T1-BASE/
cargo xtask metal run -- cargo run -p overdrive-control-plane --bin netns_density_benchmark --features integration-tests -- --profile t1-port4 --out target/benchmarks/netns-density-295/T1-PORT4/
cargo xtask lima run -- cargo check --workspace --all-targets --features integration-tests
cargo xtask lima run -- cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --features integration-tests -- -D warnings
steps.implementation_notes: Property-based tests (proptest) and state-delta thinking (assert on a declared universe of what changed vs. what's asserted unchanged) take priority over single-example unit tests where the contract supports it; integration/E2E stays single-example since it verifies wiring, not invariants.
